newsitem.title: POLAND: PBR targets issue at strategic investors.
newsitem.headline: PBR targets issue at strategic investors.

text.p: Poland's Polish Development Bank SA (PBR) wants its planned 8.4-million-share issue to attract strategic investors and help finance the bank's participation in a planned banking-insurance group, PBR's deputy head said.

"We want to address the larger part of the issue to foreign and domestic financial investors...and proceeds from the issue should be used in the process of the consolidation and privatisation of the banking sector," Piotr Cyburt told a news conference on Wednesday.

Cyburt said the bank, which now has 14,072,600 shares outstanding and is 29.5-percent owned by the state treasury, saw the strategic investor or investors gaining about a 20- percent PBR stake in the offering and increasing the bank's access to domestic andd foreign markets.
A foreign investor would provide investment banking expertise, he said.
Cyburt said the planned smaller retail tranche would primarily be aimed at improving the liqudity of PBR shares.
"The retail tranche is meant to increase the liquidity of the stock on the exchange...so it would not be so prone to speculation and large price swings," he said.

Cyburt said PBR had been in talks on forming a group with Bank Przemyslowo-Handlowy SA, Powszechny Bank Kredytowy SA which holds 33 percent of BPR, Kredyt Bank and Warta SA, in which it would specialise in investment banking.
He said PBR was interested in buying up to 15 percent of PBK in the latter bank's privatisation due later this year.
PBR's planned issue must be approved by shareholders at a meeting set for February 28.
Cyburt also said PBR expected to make a pre-tax profit of 43.2 million zlotys this year, slighty down from 1996's 47.2 million zlotys when pre-tax profit had increased by 32 percent from 1995.
